model.summary: Deep-read of /home/lab/workspace/learning/projects/sci-demographic-collapse/src/sci_demographic_collapse/emergent.py (718 lines) plus interventions.py and coremodel.py context. The behavioural core carries a 7-component state per region - C (coupling/partnership), rv=rho (permanent childlessness), Pb=Pbar (parity), tau (mean birth age), S (economic security), N (childfree-ideal norm share), q (marriageability capital) - integrated in 4 substeps/yr (dt=0.25) and coupled to the coremodel Leslie age-structure layer with zero migration and a fixed 0.3%/yr mortality improvement. TFR per agent/year = quantum * fec * tempo where quantum = C*(1-rho)*Pbar, fec(tau) = exp(-0.03*max(tau-30,0)), tempo = max(1 - 0.6*dtau, 0) with dtau the REALIZED annual post-clip change of tau (E40 fix; in run_ens the factor may exceed 1 for advancing births, bounded ~1.6 by dynamics). Calibration today anchors ONLY on the 2023 (TFR, mean-birth-age) pair in REAL: PB0 is an exact algebraic identity PB0 = TFR/(C0*(1-RV0)*fec(mab)) and PB_SCALE_ENS is the single fitted free parameter per region (re-solved by calibrate_ens so the dispersed ensemble baseline reproduces 2023 TFR exactly). C0, RV0, S0, NORM0 are hand-set judgment (NORM0 is snapped exactly to a norm-well, 0.14 or 0.42, per basin assignment); SIGMA_CAL is declared 'grounded structural heterogeneity, NOT fit'; the ~29 PARAMS rate constants are internal campaign calibrations (E19/E25/E30), not fit to external series. The production scorer is run_cal = run_ens(sigma=SIGMA_CAL, K=64, pb_scale=PB_SCALE_ENS). Rich checkable trajectories (tau path, rho path, S path, age pyramid, births, deaths, dependency ratio, per-agent TFR distribution, quantum/fec/tempo decomposition) are computed internally every year but NOT returned - the natural targets for extending calibration. Interventions enter as a 9-channel forcing (fS, fC, fPb, fTau, fRV, fN, fq, fF, fScar); interventions.py holds a 187-entry CATALOGUE on that interface.

anchors.name: REAL
anchors.meaning: 2023 calibration target pair per region: (TFR, mean age at birth). NOTE an internal label conflict: the header comment (line 29) calls the second element 'mean age at first birth', but the Poland comment says 'age-at-childbearing 29.9 from the same UN WPP series' and the Israel comment says 'MAC 30.9' - so the numbers appear to be UN WPP mean age at CHILDBEARING, not first birth; a calibration researcher must resolve which observable this is before adding age anchors. This pair is the ONLY external data anchor in the model: it sets PB0, the tau start value and tau equilibrium target, and the PB_SCALE_ENS refit target.
anchors.provenance: data-derived - UN WPP 2023 for all regions except Poland TFR which is GUS 1.16 (WPP says 1.30; GUS 2024 fell to 1.099); Korea 0.72 consistent with KOSIS; Israel UN WPP 2.83 (CBS 2.85 agrees per comment)

anchors.name: C0
anchors.meaning: Coupling (partnership/marriage propensity) start value AND baseline equilibrium: appears both as initial state and as the anchor of Ceq = C0 + gS_C*(S-S0) + gqC*q + fC - secC*100*tn. Observable counterpart: partnership/union prevalence in reproductive ages.
anchors.provenance: hand-set judgment - no data citation in code; only Israel carries a rationale comment ('near-universal marriage/partnership + familism -> highest coupling well')
anchors.values: USA 0.90; France 0.95; Germany 0.86; Italy 0.83; Japan 0.80; Korea 0.52; Poland 0.82; Israel 0.97

anchors.name: RV0
anchors.meaning: Permanent-childlessness share (rho) start value and baseline target of the drv relaxation. Observable counterpart: cohort childlessness at end of reproductive ages.
anchors.provenance: hand-set judgment - only Israel commented ('among the lowest permanent childlessness in the developed world')
anchors.values: USA 0.07; France 0.07; Germany 0.09; Italy 0.10; Japan 0.10; Korea 0.08; Poland 0.10; Israel 0.05

anchors.name: S0
anchors.meaning: Economic-security index start value (0-1) and baseline target of dS; also the reference point in the security->coupling term gS_C*(S-S0), the security->tempo term gTau*(S0-S), and the security->childlessness term -0.05*(S-S0). No direct observable named; an index needing an operationalisation (housing cost, income stability...) to become checkable.
anchors.provenance: hand-set judgment - only Israel commented ('strong familial/kin support offsets high cost of living')
anchors.values: USA 0.58; France 0.62; Germany 0.52; Italy 0.45; Japan 0.45; Korea 0.40; Poland 0.45; Israel 0.58

anchors.name: NORM0
anchors.meaning: Share endorsing a childfree ideal (norm state N) at start; each region is snapped EXACTLY to one of the two stable wells of the cubic double-well (Nlo=0.14 untrapped, Nhi=0.42 trapped) so baseline N is a fixed point and the norm->rho coupling lam_rho*(N-NORM0) is identically zero at 2023. So NORM0 encodes a binary basin assignment, not a measured survey share - survey childfree-ideal data would be the natural observable to check the assignment and the well positions.
anchors.provenance: hand-set - structurally constrained to equal Nlo or Nhi (E25)
anchors.values: low well 0.14: USA, France, Germany, Israel; high well 0.42: Italy, Japan, Korea, Poland

anchors.name: SIGMA_CAL
anchors.meaning: Per-channel population-heterogeneity spread (Latin-hypercube marginal SD) for the Phase-2 dispersed ensemble; comment declares these 'grounded, structural... NOT fit parameters' (age-at-first-birth SD ~3yr, parity intentions widest, coupling/childlessness tight). Only tau's 3.0yr is tied to a named empirical quantity; the others are judgment scaled.
anchors.provenance: hand-set / literature-informed (tau SD ~3yr cited in comment; no sources for the rest)
anchors.values: C 0.05; rv 0.03; Pb 0.15; tau 3.0; S 0.10; N 0.06; q 0.10 (scalar, shared across regions)

anchors.name: PB_SCALE_ENS
anchors.meaning: THE one calibration free parameter per region: multiplicative parity rescale re-solved by calibrate_ens() (4-iteration fixed point on a years=1 run) so the SIGMA_CAL-dispersed K=64 ensemble baseline reproduces the 2023 REAL TFR exactly under the corrected E40 B-F term. Applied as pb_scale on PB0 in run_cal.
anchors.provenance: fit - to the single 2023 TFR number per region (internal fixed-point, regenerate via calibrate_ens())
anchors.values: USA 1.0267; France 1.0286; Germany 1.0239; Italy 1.0164; Japan 1.0197; Korea 1.0176; Poland 1.0336; Israel 1.0373

anchors.name: PB0 (derived in __init__, not a literal dict)
anchors.meaning: Parity constant per region: PB0 = REAL_TFR / (C0*(1-RV0)*fec(mab)) - the algebraic identity that makes the scalar model reproduce 2023 TFR at its start state. Inherits all the hand-set uncertainty of C0/RV0: any error in those is silently absorbed into Pbar. Observable counterpart: completed parity of mothers.
anchors.provenance: fit (exact identity given REAL + hand-set C0, RV0)
anchors.values: computed at runtime from the dicts above; e.g. Korea = 0.72/(0.52*0.92*fec(32.9))

anchors.name: SIGMA0 (class attr)
anchors.meaning: All-zero per-channel dispersion default for run_ens - the baseline-preservation guarantee that sigma->0 reproduces scalar run() to machine precision.
anchors.values: C, rv, Pb, tau, S, N, q all 0.0

anchors.name: PARAMS.kS = 0.06
anchors.meaning: Security relaxation rate: dS = kS*(S0 + fS - dep_pen - S) - secS
anchors.provenance: fit - internal E19 campaign calibration (per header comment), not external data

anchors.name: PARAMS.secS = 0.0010
anchors.meaning: Secular security erosion - constant per-substep drain on S

anchors.name: PARAMS.dep_fb = 0.22
anchors.meaning: Dependency->security feedback gain: dep_pen = dep_fb * max(dep - dep0, 0) where dep = pop(65+)/pop(20-64) from the live Leslie pyramid and dep0 is the 2023 value - the channel through which ageing suppresses S. Old-age dependency ratio is a directly observable series (checkable).

anchors.name: PARAMS.kC = 0.08
anchors.meaning: Coupling relaxation rate toward Ceq = C0 + gS_C*(S-S0) + gqC*q + fC - secC*100*tn

anchors.name: PARAMS.gS_C = 0.9
anchors.meaning: Security->coupling gain in Ceq

anchors.name: PARAMS.gqC = 0.9
anchors.meaning: Marriageability-capital->coupling gain in Ceq (E30 addition)

anchors.name: PARAMS.secC = 0.0007
anchors.meaning: Secular coupling drift; enters as secC*100*tn with tn=yr/100, i.e. a linearly growing drag on Ceq

anchors.name: PARAMS.decl = 0.05, C_thr = 0.66, C_floor = 0.24
anchors.meaning: The soft-bistable coupling trap near the empirical TFR-1.5 ridge: extra decline term -decl * max(C_thr - C, 0) * max(C - C_floor, 0)/(C_thr - C_floor) pulls C down whenever it sits between floor and threshold - the mechanism that makes low-coupling regions (Korea C0=0.52) collapse and high-coupling ones stay healthy
anchors.provenance: fit (E19 internal; ridge location motivated by the empirical TFR-1.5 literature per docstring)

anchors.name: PARAMS.kPb = 0.05, gPb = 1.2, secPb = 0.0010
anchors.meaning: Parity channel: dPb = kPb*(PB0 + gPb*fPb - secPb*100*tn - Pb); gPb is the cash/quantum forcing gain, secPb the secular parity erosion

anchors.name: PARAMS.kTau = 0.06, gTau = 6.0, secTau = 0.006
anchors.meaning: Tempo channel: dtau_rate = kTau*(REAL_mab + gTau*(S0-S) + fTau + secTau*100*tn - tau); gTau converts security shortfall into postponement years, secTau the secular postponement drift. tau clipped to [24, 40]. Observable counterpart: the mean-age-at-birth time series (only its 2023 point is used today).

anchors.name: PARAMS.kBF = 0.6
anchors.meaning: Bongaarts-Feeney tempo coefficient: TFR factor max(1 - kBF*dtau, 0) on the realized annual post-clip change dtau = tau_t - tau_{t-1} (E40 fix - previously a substep rate-sum that overstated the term and could go negative)
anchors.provenance: fit/literature - the B-F form is literature (Bongaarts-Feeney), the 0.6 coefficient internal E19

anchors.name: PARAMS.kRV = 0.03, gRV = 0.012
anchors.meaning: Childlessness channel: drv = kRV*(RV0 + gRV*max(tau-30,0) - 0.05*(S-S0) + lam_rho*(N-NORM0) + fRV - rv); gRV converts each postponement year past 30 into extra permanent childlessness. NOTE the security coefficient 0.05 is HARDCODED in the equation, not in PARAMS. rv clipped [0, 0.6].

anchors.name: PARAMS.aN = 2.5, Nlo = 0.14, thN = 0.25, Nhi = 0.42, lam_rho = 0.30
anchors.meaning: Bistable social norm (E25): dN = -aN*(N-Nlo)*(N-thN)*(N-Nhi) + fN - cubic double-well with stable wells Nlo (untrapped) / Nhi (trapped) and unstable tipping point thN; lam_rho couples the norm deviation (N - NORM0) into the childlessness target. Well positions are global (not per-region).
anchors.provenance: hand-set / fit (E25 internal; no external survey anchoring of the well positions in code)

anchors.name: PARAMS.kq = 0.06, phi = 0.4, wF = 0.6, wScar = 0.5, gA = 0.5, lagLo = 27, lagHi = 45
anchors.meaning: Marriageability capital + intergenerational memory (E30): dq = kq*(fq + A_lag - q), q in [-1,1] gates coupling via gqC. Childhood environment env = wF*(fF + phi*q) - wScar*fScar is pushed yearly into ot.CohortMemory(childhood=18, repro_lo=lagLo, repro_hi=lagHi) - a per-cohort path integral (method of characteristics) - and A_lag = gA * mem.reproductive_mean() is the completed-childhood integral of today's 27-45yo reproductive cohorts. env is measured as deviation from intervention only, so identically zero on baseline.
anchors.values: kq 0.06; phi 0.4; wF 0.6; wScar 0.5; gA 0.5; lagLo 27; lagHi 45; childhood 18 (hardcoded)

anchors.name: PARAMS.wS = 0.3
anchors.meaning: DEAD PARAMETER - defined in PARAMS (line 142) but never referenced anywhere in the package (grep confirms sole occurrence is its definition). Presumably a dropped security-weight in the E30 childhood-env design.

anchors.name: hardcoded non-PARAMS constants
anchors.meaning: Constants embedded in code, not in PARAMS: fec decay slope 0.03/yr above age 30 (fec() and its inline copy in run_ens); mortality improvement Sx = 1-(1-Sx0)*(1-0.003)^(yr+1) i.e. 0.3%/yr shrink of the survival deficit, same for all regions; migration identically zero (leslie_step gets 0.0 * rogers_castro profile); dt=0.25 with 4 substeps/yr; ramp(s=2, d=10) - policy 0 until year start+2, full at start+12; erode() exp fade with 12yr time constant after s+d; state clips C [0.02,0.999], rv [0,0.6], Pb >= 1.0, tau [24,40], S [0.05,0.95], N [0,1], q [-1,1]; defaults years=102 (2023->2125), K=48 (run_ens) / 64 (run_cal, calibrate_ens), seed=0, Latin-hypercube via ndtri((k+0.5)/K) with seeded per-channel permutations

SOTA 'Honest limitations': 'the behavioural layer is a deliberately simplified, roughly tuned research instrument, good for ranking forces and comparing the shape of levers, not a precision predictor'; the combination law's bilinear form is exact only in the small-signal limit and only structural near the ridge

SOTA 'Honest limitations': migration held at zero for all behavioural runs (emergent.py passes 0.0*RC to leslie_step); the Rogers-Castro schedule is canonical, not fitted; buffered cases (USA, Germany) rest on elevated recent net migration the behavioural runs exclude

SOTA 'Honest limitations': no joint (multivariate) channel distributions - each channel dispersed marginally, full joint law a registered next step; the culture floor is descriptive (retention delta is a property of bounded communities, not a policy dial); national aggregate, descriptive not causal - East/West Germany unresolved, USA parameters do not transfer to the EU without a region-specific offset (E5-H19 REFUTED: EU MAE 0.42, no transfer), and 'even calibrated the model sizes mechanisms and places regions - it licenses no claim that a given policy achieves a given lever'

SOTA winning-levers preamble: 'Magnitudes are model dTFR on the triad; the model sizes a lever, it does not prove a policy achieves it'; section 4 caveat: the model lacks a marital-share gate, so France custody-lever numbers are likely overstated

README: 'mature exploratory research... a validated skeleton under a deliberately simplified muscle'; step 8 of the method: 'the demographic backbone reproduces real history and ranks every country correctly, while the behavioural layer that turns life conditions into a birth rate is a deliberately simplified, roughly-tuned picture, not a precision instrument'; NOTE boxes: 'not a crystal ball, forecasts no nation's future to the decimal place' and 'the model and the narrative around it are the subjective view of the researcher, not a settled forecast'

Experiments doc standing rule: 'even calibrated, the log is descriptive; it sizes mechanisms and places regions but licenses no intervention'; header: 'All hypotheses are observational... interventions are parked, not tested' (E1-E5 era) and 'Not tested - causal identification of any single intervention'

Backtest limit (E9-H30, E12-H43): population is point-predictable, period TFR only interval-predictable - a post-2015 regime change is intrinsically unforecastable from period rates; honesty is bought by widening the band to 100% coverage, not by better points

2023-anchor-only statements: emergent.py line 28 comments the REAL dict as '2023 calibration targets (TFR, mean age at first birth) and channel start values'; SOTA Calibration section anchors the behavioural baseline to 'real 2023 TFR... to under 1e-4'; E40 names the emergent core's validation surface as the 2023 anchor + baseline dynamics + the coremodel-only crisis battery. C0/RV0/S0/NORM0 carry inline justifying comments for Israel only ('near-universal marriage... highest coupling well', 'among the lowest permanent childlessness', etc.) but no citations or numeric sources anywhere

E40 DOCUMENTED (not fixed) findings that bound the anchor's precision: A5 seed wobble +/-0.006-0.009 TFR at year 1 (production pins seed 0, verdicts are same-seed deltas); A6 LHC spread clips asymmetrically near channel bounds (Israel C -0.009 with 18/64 atoms at the 0.999 ceiling, USA tau +0.038 with 24 at the floor - level absorbed by PB_SCALE_ENS); A7 tempo profile shift integer-rounded in the scalar core (smoothed by the K=64 tau spread in production)

Hardcoded model-internal choices with no observable: mortality improvement 0.3%/yr (emergent run loop), dependency ratio defined as 65+/(20-64), fec decay rate 0.03 above age 30, secular drift constants secC/secPb/secTau/secS, dep_fb=0.22, all E19 'calibrated' rate constants kC/kPb/kTau/kRV/kS and gains gS_C/gPb/gTau/gRV/gqC

Known omissions logged since E1-E5: migration the largest (E5-H20: adding it cuts the USA population residual 85%); the technology-coupling mechanism failed its out-of-sample bar (E4-H17, 17% vs required 25%); recession magnitude under-reproduced (E3-H9 REFUTED, model 0.14 vs observed 0.26); house-price series never ingested (E3-H13 INCONCLUSIVE)

The old model's crude-marriage-rate MAPE 8.0% target (E1-H4) was never carried over to the emergent C channel

S0 economic-security anchors (0.40-0.62): the Seldon manifold's entire y-axis, hand-set. Target: a documented composite of observables - youth (25-34) unemployment/NEET rate, housing-cost-to-income for young adults, age at leaving parental home (Eurostat), relative income of young adults vs national median - so each region's S0 becomes reproducible from named series

Tempo-mirage magnitudes (post-E40: Korea fTau=-3 peak +0.07): now that E40 deflated them 4x, the corrected amplitudes can be held against measured tempo effects - the Bongaarts-Feeney decompositions of real episodes the log already cites as text (Hungary's post-2010 tempo rebound, the Czech 2000s recuperation, H74/H113/H160-class rows quote Hungarian/Alaskan decompositions as real-world numbers, never as model output). A quantitative model-vs-measured tempo-bump comparison is absent

Mean-age-at-childbearing trajectory: the model integrates tau forward with a secular drift (secTau) but MAC is never scored after 2023. Target: observed MAC 2024-2025 per region (WPP revisions, NCHS births data, GUS, KOSIS, CBS) - the cheapest new held-out test available, and the code's own REAL comment ambiguity ('mean age at FIRST birth' vs coremodel's MAC = mean age at childbearing; values 29.4-32.9 are MAC-like) needs resolving before anchoring

2024-2025 TFR as rolling held-out data: the emergent.py comment already records GUS 2024 Poland = 1.099; Korea 2024 (KOSIS) ticked up; every region has a post-anchor TFR print the baseline trajectory could be scored against - turning the single 2023 anchor into an annually extending backtest of the behavioural layer itself

Quantum claims (E8-H27: USA quantum 2.18 near replacement, Korea 1.55 structural; E13 qualified 'the USA quantum is itself eroding'): completed cohort fertility from the Human Fertility Database for cohorts now finishing (born ~1975-1985) is the direct observable the tempo-quantum split predicts

Coupling-collapse trajectory in Korea (README: partnership decline as THE driver; SOTA E19 'Korea collapses alone'): the model emits a C(t) path that is never compared to Korea's observed marriage-rate/ever-married-by-age collapse (KOSIS series) - the one channel trajectory where excellent annual data exists

The housing-fission claims (E38/E39: household demand +27% by 2100 from coupling decline alone, h = 1 - c/2, fission crossing 2062): checkable near-term against official household-projection series (KOSIS household projections, Eurostat household forecasts) which embody measured headship rates - a direct test of the h = 1 - c/2 identity and the loop's early trajectory

The 1.5 ridge as an out-of-sample classifier: SOTA validates placement against the Lutz threshold, but historical recoveries and non-recoveries (Czechia 1.13->1.83, Germany 1.24->1.59, vs Italy/Japan staying trapped) form a labelled test set for the trap's central prediction that basin position decides recoverability - none are currently scored

Israel sub-population floor (E33/E35 replicator, floor ~4.3-6.8 over four generations, retention delta the load-bearing axis): the code comment already carries the composition numbers (Haredi 6.38, secular 1.98, Arab ~2.9); measured retention/apostasy rates (Pew surveys, Israel CBS religiosity-switching data) would turn delta from an assumption into an anchored parameter

fec(tau) = exp(-0.03*max(tau-30,0)): the 0.03 fecundity decay is checkable against the ART/natural-fecundability literature the project already digests; likewise dep_fb=0.22 (ageing burden -> youth security) against empirical fiscal-transfer/generational-accounting estimates (the BDJ pension-fertility digest E18 cites is adjacent)

README single-number claims that deserve a pinned source or model-run reference: '97% of Korea's 2050 births come from women already alive in 2023' (E13-C13 - pure WPP age-structure arithmetic, trivially verifiable), 'roughly two out of every three [paths] lead down into decline' (66% basin volume - a parameter-space measure with no observable; should be labelled as such), and the E36 saturation asymptote +0.487 (the near-origin slope is Autor/Kearney-anchored but the ceiling itself has no empirical anchor)

Region codes cover 11 entities incl. all 8 campaign regions (USA 840, France 250, Germany 276, Italy 380, Japan 392, Korea 410, Poland 616, Israel 376) plus China, Spain, Europe-908 - the extra three are legacy/story regions, not calibrated in emergent.py's REAL dict

What is NOT fitted in this layer: the Rogers-Castro schedule (canonical constants), the migration totals in behavioural runs (zeroed), and the mortality-improvement rate used by emergent.py's forward runs (hardcoded 0.3%/yr on top of the last observed Sx)

The file also provides the analysis operators the campaign's structural claims rest on: build_leslie/leslie_spectrum (eigenstructure), keyfitz_momentum (NRR=1 rescale projection), nrr, and the mape() panel-metric helper

Terminology flag worth fixing before extending calibration: the REAL dict comment says 'mean age at first birth' but the values (USA 29.4, Korea 32.9, Israel 30.9) and the coremodel MAC indicator are mean age at childbearing; README step 2 says 'mean age at childbearing'. Any new tau anchor must pick one definition (MAC vs MAB1 differ by ~2-3 years) and name its series

Two structural quantities that look calibrated but are not: PB_SCALE_ENS is the one genuinely fitted free parameter per region (re-solved by calibrate_ens after E40), and it silently absorbs whatever the hand-set anchors get wrong (E40-A6 says so explicitly - 'the level is absorbed by PB_SCALE_ENS'). Because PB0 is solved FROM C0/RV0/S0, errors in the hand-set anchors do not show up as a 2023 TFR residual at all - they re-appear only as mis-attributed channel decompositions (e.g. the E37 coupling-vs-norm transplant split). This is why per-channel observables are the highest-value extension: the current anchor cannot detect a wrong C0 compensated by a wrong PB0

The apparent tension between SOTA's 'nearly three in ten women never having a child' (Germany/Italy/Japan, E15) and RV0 = 0.09-0.10 in code suggests RV0 is a different construct (current-stock or annualised rate) than cohort childlessness; whichever it is, its definition is undocumented - resolving that definition is prerequisite to anchoring it

targets.definition: Share of women with zero live-born (biological) children at the end of reproductive life, target cohorts born ~1965-1978. Measurement age is region-specific (40 Korea-supplementary, 40-44 Poland, 45-49/50-54 Germany, 45-50 USA, 49 Italy, 50 Japan, 45-59 Israel, cohort-complete France); never-married women counted childless where parity is asked only of ever-married (Korea census). Shares as fractions 0-1.
targets.model_mapping: Pins the composition 1 - C0*(1-RV0): in emergent.py TFR = C*(1-rho)*Pbar*fec*tempo, so the model share of women never entering motherhood is 1 - C*(1-rho); at the 2023 anchor state that is 1 - C0*(1-RV0). Arithmetic check of the hand-set anchors against these observations: USA 0.163 vs obs 0.165 (close); Germany 0.217 vs 0.20-0.21 (close); Italy 0.253 vs 0.230 (close); Japan 0.280 vs 0.27-0.28 (dead on); Israel 0.0785 vs 0.078 (dead on); France 0.117 vs 0.14 (model undershoots); Poland 0.262 vs 0.103-0.15 (model far above observation); Korea 0.522 vs 0.072-0.19 rising to 0.267 for the 1980 cohort at 40 (model far above completed-cohort observation - C0=0.52 encodes the projected 2023 partnership state, not completed-cohort behaviour). Mapping algebra is done downstream.

targets.model_mapping: Pins the completed-cohort quantum C0*(1-RV0)*PB0 (the model's quantum = C*(1-rho)*Pbar integrated over the cohort's realized fec(tau) path). targets.model_mapping: Pins the model's tau observable (mean birth age): MAB1 fixes the entry-into-motherhood LEVEL and, via the 2000-2023 slope, the secular drift rate dtau that the Bongaarts-Feeney term damps TFR by (factor max(1-kBF*dtau,0), kBF=0.6). LOAD-BEARING correction: the model's only age anchor, REAL[region][1] (USA 29.4, France 31.1, Germany 31.0, Italy 31.8, Japan 31.4, Korea 32.9, Poland 29.9, Israel 30.9), is mean age at CHILDBEARING (MAC, all births), NOT first birth - confirmed because those values track WPP MAC (USA MAC 29.9, Israel MAC 30.9) and are 2-4 yr ABOVE MAB1 (USA 27.5, Israel 27.72, Poland 28.4), while only Korea/Italy nearly coincide. Consequence for calibration: if tau is meant to be entry-age (it feeds gRV childlessness for tau>30 and the fec penalty above 30), MAB1 is the faithful observable and would LOWER tau by ~2-4 yr for most regions, pulling several below the age-30 childlessness/fecundity threshold. MAC (this family's cross-check) validates the existing REAL anchor to within ~0.3-0.9 yr. The MAB1 secular rise (Korea steepest at +5.3 yr over 2000-2023 ≈ 0.23 yr/yr; Israel near-flat since 2015 ≈ 0) directly pins the per-region dtau feeding kTau/secTau/kBF.

Where the exact cut is unavailable the nearest definition is used and flagged per region: France and USA are both-sexes couple shares (USA 25-34); Germany/Italy/Poland are census legal marital status (married or registered partnership, consensual unions excluded); Japan is the census de facto with-spouse share (includes unregistered partners); Korea is women 30-39 ever-married (1 minus never-married); Israel is women 25-29 ever-married. targets.model_mapping: Pins C0 in emergent.py - the hand-set coupling start value and the anchor of the coupling equilibrium Ceq = C0 + gS_C*(S-S0) + gqC*q + fC - secC*100*tn, which multiplies TFR directly through quantum = C*(1-rho)*Pbar. Current hand-set C0 (USA .90, France .95, Germany .86, Italy .83, Japan .80, Korea .52, Poland .82, Israel .97) is VALIDATED at the extremes but MISORDERED in the middle: observed 25-39 union shares are France 0.642 (full married-or-cohabiting def) > Poland 0.607 (marriage-only; ~0.63 with its small cohabitation) > USA 0.57 (25-34) > Japan 0.535 (de facto) > Germany 0.463 (marriage-only; ~0.56-0.63 adding cohabitation per OECD SF3.3 +17.4pp at 20-34) > Italy 0.382 (marriage-only; ~0.45 with cohabitation), with Korea far lowest (women 30-39 ever-married 0.664 but 25-29 never-married rates imply a 25-39 union share well below 0.5) and Israel the earliest/most universal marriage (women 25-29 already 0.553 ever-married, never-married by 45-49 only ~11%). Agreements: Israel top (C0 .97), France top of the West (.95), Korea bottom (.52), Italy low. Contradictions: (1) Poland's observed partnership share is second-highest of the eight yet C0(PL)=.82 ranks 6th - Poland's low TFR is being explained by low coupling when its coupling is actually high, so the error is absorbed into PB0/parity via the algebraic identity PB0 = TFR/(C0*(1-RV0)*fec); (2) Japan > Italy in the data but C0 has Italy .83 > Japan .80. Recommended use: recalibrate C0 as a monotone (affine) map of the observed union share u, e.g. anchored so Israel keeps .97 and Korea its census-implied floor, then re-derive PB0/PB_SCALE_ENS; this breaks the C0-RV0-Pbar degeneracy the 2023-TFR-only calibration cannot see.

targets.definition: Share of adults of reproductive age whose personal IDEAL number of children is zero (childfree-ideal share), latest comparable wave, expressed as a fraction; companion statistic in each note = mean ideal (or desired/intended) family size. Reference operationalisations per region: USA = Gallup general-ideal question, adults 18+ (2025 wave); France/Germany/Italy/Poland = Eurobarometer 2011 personal ideal, ages 25-39, unweighted mean of the published women's and men's shares (Testa 2012 Table A.2.6), with intended-childlessness ages 18-40 (Miettinen & Szalma 2014 Table 1) in the note; Japan = pooled national-survey estimate of childfree adults 18-50 ("neither have nor want children", 2020); Korea = intended childlessness ages 20-49 (no ideal-zero measure found - flagged); Israel = no zero-share published (null).
targets.model_mapping: Pins NORM0 (childfree-ideal norm state) and its double-well geometry (Nlo=0.14 untrapped / thN=0.25 / Nhi=0.42 trapped, PARAMS aN=2.5) plus the norm-to-childlessness coupling lam_rho=0.30 in drv = kRV*(RV0 + ... + lam_rho*(N-NORM0) + ...). Data verdict: (1) ONLY Korea's observable matches a well - intended childlessness 0.426 (2024, ages 20-49) sits exactly on Nhi=0.42; (2) every other region is an order of magnitude below its assigned well: untrapped USA 0.02, France 0.015, Germany 0.075, Israel ~0 are all well under Nlo=0.14, and trapped-well Italy 0.035, Japan 0.056, Poland 0.02 are far below 0.42 and even below Nlo; (3) Poland's basin assignment is contradicted by the observable - it has among the LOWEST childfree ideals/intentions in Europe (EB2011 ideal-zero W1%/M3%; the eastern-European "at least one child" norm is documented as preserved), so its trap must be carried by S/C channels, not N; Italy is marginal (male intended-zero 9.3% rising). Consequence: either reinterpret N as a latent norm index calibrated only by ORDERING (Korea >> Germany > Japan ~ Italy > Poland ~ France ~ USA > Israel), or move the wells to data (Nlo ~0.02-0.08, Nhi ~0.43 with only Korea trapped). Scale check on lam_rho: Germany ideal-zero 0.075 vs RV0=0.09 is consistent; Korea 0.426 vs RV0=0.08 implies intended childlessness vastly exceeds realized cohort childlessness - headroom the rv clip (0.6) permits but current RV0 anchoring ignores. Mean ideals bound the Pbar quantum ceiling: Korea is the only region whose mean ideal (1.8) is itself below replacement; Israel the only one near 4 - consistent with Israel's high-coupling/low-rho hand-set anchors.

Wording and sampling effects are first-order for this observable: the Japan pooling paper shows childfree-prevalence estimates ranging 1.2-40.3% across instruments; private surveys (Rohto 55.2%) are not comparable to national statistics.

targets.definition: Bongaarts-Feeney tempo-adjusted total fertility rate (adjTFR / TFR-BF; Bongaarts & Feeney 1998): the PERIOD TFR of a single calendar year purged of the distortion from a rising mean age at childbearing, computed by birth order where available (HFD) or from total data (HFC "BF"). Not a cohort measure. Value reported = the adjTFR itself; each region is paired (in note) with its same-year raw TFR, and the tempo gap = adjTFR − TFR. Women 15-49. Most recent published year per region (varies 2016-2022). Distinct from the tempo- AND parity-adjusted TFRp* (Bongaarts-Sobotka 2012), which is flagged separately where a source uses it.
targets.model_mapping: Pins the Bongaarts-Feeney tempo coefficient PARAMS.kBF = 0.6. In emergent.py TFR = quantum·fec·max(1 − kBF·dτ, 0), so the equilibrium tempo drag equals the observed gap G = 1 − TFR/adjTFR. A sustained gap G implies a steady-state postponement rate dτ ≈ G/kBF yr⁻¹; the adjTFR−TFR pairs therefore jointly test kBF and the τ-path (kTau/gTau/secTau) dynamics. Observed gaps span ~nil (Germany 2022, −0.04) and small (USA +0.16, France +0.11, Poland +0.13) to large (Italy +0.20, Japan +0.17, Korea +0.23). Korea's +0.23 is the binding check: even tempo-corrected, its quantum (~1.0) stays far sub-replacement, so the collapse is quantum not merely tempo. adjTFR also equals the model's quantum·fec factor (TFR before the tempo term), giving a direct handle on separating quantum from tempo per region.

targets.definition: Share of persons aged 25-34 (both sexes, all marital statuses) living in the same household as at least one of their own (or their spouse's) parents, expressed as a fraction 0-1 of the age-group population. Reference year 2023 where available (EU regions via EU-SILC, USA via ACS); otherwise the latest national census/survey year (Japan 2015 Census, Israel 2018 Social Survey, Korea 2020 Census). Deviations from the 25-34 window or marital scope are flagged per region.
targets.model_mapping: Pins the hand-set S0 economic-security anchor (emergent.py S0 dict, 0.40-0.62) as an INVERSE ordinal proxy: high parental co-residence = low young-adult residential/economic independence = low S0. mappings.model_expression: Observed completed-cohort childlessness p0 maps to the model's never-mother share: p0_model = 1 - C*(1-rv). At the 2023 anchor state (run() init, emergent.py:249-259) this is the closed form p0 = 1 - C0[r]*(1-RV0[r]). In the ensemble (run_ens, :528-562) the LHC marginals are decorrelated by seeded permutations, so E_K[C_k*(1-rv_k)] = C0*(1-RV0) + O(Cov)=C0*(1-RV0) to first order - the scalar identity carries over. Dynamically, the cohort born b has p0(b) = 1 - mean_{t in [b+MAB1, b+45]} C(t)*(1-rv(t)); the researched values (cohorts 1965-1978, completing 1985-2023) therefore anchor a LAGGED window average, not the 2023 point. Arithmetic already run against the hand-set anchors: USA 0.163 vs obs 0.165, DE 0.217 vs 0.20-0.21, IT 0.253 vs 0.230, JP 0.280 vs 0.27-0.28, IL 0.0785 vs 0.078 (all close); FR 0.117 vs 0.14 (undershoot); PL 0.262 vs 0.103-0.15 and KR 0.522 vs 0.19-0.267 (far off - cohort-vs-state mismatch dominates Korea; Poland is a genuine anchor error: obs p0=0.103 < 1-C0=0.18 is INFEASIBLE at any RV0>=0, proving C0[PL] must rise to >= 0.897 on the cohort reading).

mappings.model_expression: tau IS mean age at childbearing (MAC): REAL[r][1] is tau's start value (:254) and relaxation target (:215-217, dtau_rate = kTau*(REAL[1] + gTau*(S0-S) + fTau + secTau*100*tn - tau)), and the Leslie ASFR shift uses tau - REAL[1] (:305) - all MAC semantics; the header 'mean age at first birth' comment (line 28) is mislabelled (confirmed: REAL values track WPP MAC, 2-4 yr above observed MAB1). Predicted observables: MAC_model(t) = tau(t) trajectory; baseline drift = secTau (at baseline S~S0 so the gTau term ~0; dep_pen is the only S mover) giving asymptotic target growth 0.006 yr/yr - versus observed 2000-2023 MAC/MAB1 drifts of 0.09-0.23 yr/yr, a ~20-40x tension the backtest must adjudicate (postponement plateau vs continuation). MAB1 = MAC - Delta1[r] with observed Delta1 from 0.5 yr (KR) to 3.2 yr (IL) - NOT a constant. The age-30 thresholds in fec (:157) and gRV*max(tau-30,0) (:223) are entry-age semantics applied to a MAC variable; decision required: keep tau=MAC and re-interpret thresholds as MAC-scale (recalibrated), or key them off tau - Delta1[r].

synthesis.protocol:
JOINT CALIBRATION PROTOCOL (strict order; each stage's outputs frozen before the next; every stage read-only until the user approves code changes).

STAGE 0 - definitions (no numbers move yet): (a) resolve tau = MAC and fix the line-28 label; decide the Delta1 (entry-age keying) question - recommendation: keep tau=MAC, do NOT rekey fec/gRV this round (structural change, separate experiment), record Delta1 as documentation; (b) decide Germany TFR source (recommend Destatis 1.38 per national-office convention); (c) fix the RV0 construct definition (completed-cohort childlessness at 45+, cohorts ~1972-77, Korea exception documented); (d) choose norm option A (latent ordering) vs B (well relocation) - recommendation: A this round, B as a registered structural experiment, because B forces E25-E39 verdict re-runs; (e) note wS=0.3 (line 147) is dead - flag for removal, no behaviour change.

STAGE 1 - static anchor replacement (closed-form, no optimizer): solve in this order because each feeds the next: (1) REAL[r][1] <- WPP-on-disk MAC 2023; (2) C0 <- two-point affine of harmonized union share u (endpoints Korea 0.52, Israel 0.97 preserved; Poland and Japan/Italy interior corrections); (3) RV0 <- 1-(1-p0_obs)/C0 with Korea as a bounded interval; (4) PB0 recomputes automatically via the line-196 identity - then compute PB0_check from CFR and REPORT the residual per region (target: |PB0-PB0_check|/PB0 < 10%; larger = the quantum composition itself is wrong for that region, log it, do not tune it away); (5) NORM0 per the Stage-0 decision; (6) S0 <- co-residence composite (gauge - touches nothing downstream, purely documentary + transplant validity). No loss function in this stage: these are exact identities and documented maps, which is the point - each anchor has ONE named source and ONE formula.

STAGE 2 - re-anchor the ensemble: rerun calibrate_ens() (emergent.py:637-650, 4-iteration fixed point on years=1, K=64, SIGMA_CAL unchanged - it is declared structural and this round does not earn the right to touch it) to regenerate PB_SCALE_ENS; acceptance: 2023 TFR reproduced < 1e-4 for 8/8 (the existing bar) AND |PB_SCALE_ENS-1| does not grow for any region vs the committed values (1.0164-1.0373).

STAGE 3 - dynamics against series (the only optimizer stage): free parameters GLOBAL ONLY: {secC, secPb, secTau} and optionally {kTau} - four scalars against an 8-region panel; everything else FIXED: kBF=0.6 (literature, swept - Stage 4 may move it within {0.4..1.0}), trap (decl, C_thr, C_floor) fixed and VALIDATED by the Korea-only-firing criterion, kC/kPb/kS/kRV/gS_C/gTau/gRV/lam_rho/aN/dep_fb and all E30 constants fixed, SIGMA_CAL fixed, Leslie layer untouched. Loss: weighted least squares over the backtest window, L = sum_r sum_t w_TFR*[(TFR_m - TFR_o)/s_TFR]^2 + w_MAC*[(tau_m - MAC_o)/s_MAC]^2 + w_M*[(Chat_m - mhat_o)/s_M]^2 with s_TFR = 0.03 (source noise + revision spread), s_MAC = 0.15 yr, s_M = 5% relative on the normalized marriage index; weights w = 1/1/0.5 (marriage down-weighted for the flow-vs-stock and cohabitation biases); years 2020-2022 excluded (COVID, documented as such); Poland scored on GUS, Korea on KOSIS, never the WPP rows for those two. Fit by coarse grid then local refinement - 4 params, no gradient machinery needed; every candidate is one run per region per year-window.

STAGE 4 - kBF adjudication: score the frozen Stage-3 system's quantum*fec trajectory against published adjTFR levels (7 regions, Israel null) for kBF in {0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0}; keep 0.6 unless a value outside the E40 sweep band wins by more than the adjTFR volatility (+-0.1); if kBF moves, return to Stage 2 (PB_SCALE_ENS refit) once - the loop converges because kBF only touches the tempo factor.

STAGE 5 - re-verdict gate: recompute the campaign's standing headline numbers (E37 transplant split, basin table, Seldon placements) under the new anchors; any hypothesis whose verdict rides on a flipped basin or a re-ranked C0 (Poland, Japan/Italy) goes on the re-run list - recalibration does NOT silently retire recorded verdicts. PB_SCALE_ENS interaction, stated once: it is always re-solved LAST, it always absorbs the residual level, and the protocol's honesty metric is that it has LESS to absorb - report the per-region |scale-1| trajectory across stages in the final table.
