OBSERVABILITY HARNESS (additive - existing return keys unchanged so no downstream notebook breaks; spec only, implementation on approval).

(1) Trajectory exposure. run(), run_dist(), run_ens()/run_cal() gain a `trajectories` dict (per-year, length `years`): all seven channels C, rv, Pb, tau, S, N, q (ensemble MEAN in run_ens; run() already returns C/TFR/N/q - add rv, Pb, tau, S); the TFR decomposition as separate arrays quantum_t = mean(C*(1-rv)*Pb), fec_t = mean(exp(-0.03*clip(tau-30,0,None))), tempo_t = mean(clip(1-kBF*(tau-tau_prev),0,None)), dtau_t = mean(tau-tau_prev), adjTFR_t = mean over agents of quantum_i*fec_i (the tempo-free per-agent product - the object published adjTFR maps to); Leslie observables currently computed and discarded: births_t and deaths_t (the `_b, _d` bindings at :300/:427/:603 - annual births are the most-published vital statistic in every region), totpop_t, dep_t (65+/20-64, :312) and dep_pen_t (the feedback channel, checkable against observed dependency series); A_lag_t and env_t (the E30 memory path). Optional pyramid snapshots (nf, nm) every 5 years for 2024-2025 pyramid validation.

(2) Ensemble spread exposure. Per-year std of tfr_i and of each channel (currently only the final-year dist_end exists, :633-634); dist snapshots at years {1, 27, 52, 77, end} so the heterogeneity claims are inspectable mid-path, not only at the end.

(3) The predicted-vs-observed table (the deliverable every parameter must appear in). One machine-readable table (reports/calibration_targets.csv is the natural home next to nb7_parameter_table.csv), one row per (region x observable x year): columns = observable_id, model_expression (the exact formula, e.g. '1 - C0*(1-RV0)'), model_key (which harness key produces it, e.g. trajectories.adjTFR_t[2022]), model_value, observed_value, observed_source (named series + URL), observed_sigma, residual, residual_over_sigma, parameter_pinned. Rows enumerated: 2023 TFR (existing anchor) per region; 2024-2025 TFR out-of-sample per region as published (GUS 1.099/1.068, KOSIS 0.75, Destatis 1.35, Eurostat FR/IT/DE); MAC 2023 level + 2024 prints vs tau_t; MAB1 2023 vs tau_t - Delta1 (documentation row if Delta1 not adopted); cohort childlessness vs 1-C0*(1-RV0) (lagged-window caveat column); CFR-1975 and parity-of-mothers vs C0(1-RV0)PB0*fec and PB0*fec; union share u vs C0 (through the affine map, map stated in the row); adjTFR vs adjTFR_t (7 regions); normalized marriage index vs C_t/C_0 (witness row, upper-bound semantics flagged); childfree share vs N_t (ordering-only under option A); co-residence vs S0 map (documentation row - gauge flagged); annual births 2024-2025 vs births_t; old-age dependency ratio (observed WPP/Eurostat) vs dep_t. Every PARAMS constant the protocol frees or validates (secC, secPb, secTau, kTau, kBF, decl/C_thr/C_floor) must appear in at least one row's parameter_pinned column - that is the completeness check for 'predictions checkable per parameter'; constants with NO row (kS, kRV, gRV, gPb, aN, dep_fb, kq and the E30 block, fec slope 0.03, mortality 0.3%/yr) are listed in a companion 'unanchored constants' section of the table so the surface's boundary is explicit rather than implied.
synthesis.backtest_plan:
2000-2023 BACKTEST (a rejection test, not a fitting exercise - Stage 3 of the protocol supplies the only 3-4 fitted scalars).

INITIALIZATION (the honest hard part - the model starts at 2023 by construction, run() :249-259): build a 2000-era start state per region from the same observable families, same sources, earlier vintages: tau(2000) = WPP MAC 2000 (on disk in demographic_indicators.csv); C(2000) from the partnership map applied to 2000-era union data where it exists, else back-projected from the normalized marriage index (documented as weaker); rv(2000) from cohort childlessness of cohorts completing ~2000 (born ~1955-60: USA ~0.16, DE ~0.21 (b.1963-67 plateau), JP 0.116 (b.1943-47) -> interpolate, KR 0.072 (b.1965) - the Korea gradient is itself information); Pb(2000) from the line-196 identity evaluated with the 2000 TFR and 2000-state C/rv; S(2000) = S0 (gauge - dep_pen(2000) re-based to the 2000 pyramid, which the Leslie layer already loads from y0=1990); N(2000) = assigned well (norms move slowly; under option A this is the latent index); q(2000) = 0 (env is intervention-only by construction, :291-293). Leslie side starts from the observed 2000 pyramids already in data/raw/unwpp (load_unwpp spans 1990-2023). Where a 2000 state cell cannot be sourced, solve it by shooting to the 2023 anchor and MARK that region-channel as circular (it then contributes shape information only, not level).

EXECUTION: integrate 2000->2023 (years=23) with zero forcing; production configuration (run_cal semantics: SIGMA_CAL, K=64, seed 0) plus a scalar run() for interpretability; harness trajectories on.

SCORING (three tiers): Tier 1 point series - TFR(t) vs the family-8 series under the source conventions (GUS Poland including the 2017 peak 1.453; KOSIS Korea including the 2012 local peak; WPP others; Germany per the Stage-0 source decision), MAC(t) vs WPP MAC, normalized marriage index vs C(t)/C(2000); metric = per-region MAE with the sigma bands from the protocol; 2020-2022 excluded. Tier 2 feature tests (pass/fail, these carry the verdict): Korea's 2015->2023 halving reproduced with the trap term active - AND the trap term integrates to ~0 for the other seven in-window (the Korea-only-firing criterion; print the trap term's yearly value from the harness); Israel flat at ~2.9-3.1 throughout (null control - any secular slide there falsifies the drift triple); Germany's 2005-2016 rise (sign change - if the global drifts cannot produce it, record that the model lacks the mechanism rather than adding one); Japan's double sign change (same treatment); Italy's monotone slide matched within band (the clean drift test). Tier 3 out-of-sample - freeze everything at the 2023 anchor, run 2 years forward, score the published 2024-2025 prints (TFR: GUS 1.099/1.068, KOSIS 0.75, Destatis 1.35, Eurostat FR 1.61(p)/IT 1.18/DE 1.36; MAC/MAB1 2024 where published: KR MAB1 33.08, PL 28.7, DE 29.9, FR 29.3; births 2024 where published) - this turns the single 2023 anchor into an annually extending held-out test, the cheapest permanent upgrade of the whole plan; Korea's 2024 marriage upturn (+14.8%) is logged as a standing C-dynamics stress point (a monotone-decay baseline cannot produce it - if KOSIS 2025-2026 sustains the upturn, the Korea no-forcing baseline is falsified and that is a finding, not an embarrassment).

DISCIPLINE: one loss evaluation per candidate parameter vector, no per-region drift tuning; every excluded year, circular init cell, and failed feature test goes in the experiments log verbatim; the E10 crisis battery is untouched (it lives entirely in coremodel per E40) so this backtest extends the surface to the behavioural layer without double-counting the Leslie validations.
risks: Cohort-to-state lag is the deepest measurement mismatch: childlessness/CFR describe cohorts born 1965-78 completing 1985-2023, not the 2023 period state; in Korea the within-window cohort gradient (childlessness 0.072->0.267) exceeds the entire signal, so KR RV0/C0 remain interval-bounded judgment even after 'data-deriving' - claiming otherwise would be false precision.

The partnership harmonisation gap: DE/IT/PL are marriage-only census values with 2011-vintage cohabitation top-ups, KR/IL are ever-married complements on the wrong age windows; the affine C0 map inherits +-0.05-0.10 interior error until the KOSIS 25-39 cut and CBS age tables are fetched - interior C0 values must not be quoted to better than +-0.05.

S0 is a gauge at baseline (only S-S0 deviations enter the dynamics), so no data in this plan can FIT it - the deliverable is an operationalisation, and any doc language saying S0 became 'calibrated' would overclaim. Same for aN (needs a norm time series that does not exist) and for gTau/gS_C at baseline (identified only through crisis excursions, weakly).

Norm option B (well relocation) is a structural change wearing calibration's clothes: flipping Poland (and possibly Italy/Japan) out of the trapped well changes intervention geometry and invalidates E25-E39 norm-verdicts for the flipped regions - budget a verdict re-run campaign or stay with option A; conversely option A leaves Nhi=0.42 pinned by ONE intention-scale survey (KPPIF via Korea Herald) whose wording reads high versus ideal-zero.

Backtest degeneracy and circularity: secC/secPb trade off on monotone declines (split only via the marriage witness and CFR gap, both biased in known directions); 2000 initial-state cells solved by shooting to 2023 make those regions' paths partially circular; and 8 regions x ~20 usable years can genuinely identify only ~3-4 global scalars - the temptation to add per-region drifts to pass Tier-2 feature tests (Germany's hump, Japan's double sign change) must be refused and logged as missing mechanisms.

PB_SCALE_ENS remains the silent absorber: after re-anchoring, if |scale-1| grows instead of shrinking the exercise has re-labelled the error, not removed it - the protocol makes this the headline diagnostic, but it only works if the number is actually reported per stage.

Source-convention fractures: Germany TFR (WPP 1.44 vs Destatis 1.35-1.38) moves the region relative to the 1.5 ridge and thus basin proximity; Poland's Leslie ASFR shape stays WPP while its TFR is GUS; Korea/Israel CFRs are WPP diagonals (not independent of the model's own data backbone); tempo-adjusted TFR mixes two indicator variants (BF vs TFRp*) and two vintages that disagree on Germany's gap sign; Israel has no adjTFR at all - the null-control region is unscored on the tempo family.

The Delta1/entry-age decision is a hidden structural fork: keying fec/gRV off MAB1 instead of MAC switches the tau>30 terms OFF at 2023 for five regions (USA/FR/DE/PL/IL) - deferring it (as recommended) means the childlessness channel keeps running on MAC semantics that the age-30 threshold was arguably not written for; this must be carried as a documented limitation, not forgotten.

Secular-drift tension is large and known in advance: observed 2000-2023 postponement runs 0.09-0.23 yr/yr against the model's secTau=0.006 target drift - if Stage 3 resolves this by inflating secTau ~20x, forward runs to 2125 will extrapolate postponement implausibly (tau clips at 40, :234); a saturating drift may be needed, which is again a structural change beyond this round's mandate.

Operational risks: the harness must be strictly additive (36 notebooks and reports/*.json key off current return signatures); trajectory exposure at K=64 x 102 years x 8 regions grows memory/report size; and several load-bearing gap-fills (KOSIS parity and 25-39 marital cut, CBS childlessness for younger cohorts and adjTFR, GUS NSP cohort childlessness, HFD auth-gated parity tables) are fetch tasks that can silently slip - each null cell in the predicted-vs-observed table must stay visible as null rather than being back-filled by judgment.

critiques.verdict: MAJOR REVISIONS REQUIRED before any code is touched. The data layer is solid: every locally recomputable number was independently re-derived and matches (WPP cohort-1975 diagonals, MAC 2023, TFR series points from data/raw/unwpp; Eurostat/census weighted union shares re-add exactly; the 1-C0*(1-RV0) arithmetic reproduces for all 8 regions; wS at emergent.py:147 is confirmed dead). The synthesis layer, however, contains one blocking internal contradiction - Stage 1 derives C0 from a 25-39 period partnership STOCK and then RV0 from LIFETIME cohort childlessness, a pair that is jointly infeasible (negative RV0) for most of the panel - plus several stage-level design errors: an unwinnable Stage-4 adjTFR level test given the PB0 identity, a cohort-vs-period epoch mismatch built into the PB0_check acceptance bar, a mis-specified honesty metric (PB_SCALE_ENS absorbs the Jensen gap, not anchor error), a Poland infeasibility 'proof' riding on the family's weakest number, a trapped norm well pinned by a definitionally incomparable intention survey, and unhandled collisions with the E40 pytest guard suite. None of this is fatal to the mandate - the observables are the right ones - but the protocol must be re-ordered around one consistent construct for C and epoch-matched comparisons before Stage 1 executes.

findings.item: Stage 1 steps (2)+(3) are jointly infeasible: C0 = affine(union share u, endpoints Korea 0.52 / Israel 0.97) followed by RV0 = 1-(1-p0)/C0 yields NEGATIVE RV0 for most regions
findings.why: Feasibility requires C0 >= 1-p0 (USA 0.835, FR 0.86, DE ~0.80, IT 0.77, PL 0.897, IL 0.922), but the affine maps the observed 25-39 stocks (USA 0.57, FR 0.642, DE 0.56-0.63, IT ~0.45, JP 0.535, PL ~0.63) to ~0.65-0.85 for any plausible endpoints - e.g. USA RV0 = 1-0.835/0.72 < 0. Root cause is a construct clash the synthesis never names: the never-mother identity 1-C(1-rv)=p0 requires C to be the LIFETIME ever-partnered share (which is what the current hand-set C0 0.80-0.97 actually track, explaining why 5 of 8 arithmetic checks are 'close'), while the partnership family measures a point-in-time 25-39 STOCK (women un-partnered at 30 mostly partner later). Two families pin the same symbol to two different observables and the protocol chains them as if compatible.
findings.fix: Pick ONE construct for C - recommend lifetime ever-in-union by end of reproductive life (never-married/never-partnered complements at 45-49 from census tables: the Israel note already carries 'never-married women 45-49 ~11%'), and demote the 25-39 stock to a trend/ordering witness for the C dynamics only. Then derive (C0, RV0) jointly from {p0_cohort, lifetime-partnership} with the feasibility constraint explicit, instead of sequentially. Rewrite the mapping algebra and Stage 1 order before anything executes.

findings.item: Stage 4 (kBF adjudication by scoring model quantum*fec against published adjTFR LEVELS) is unwinnable as specified
findings.why: The PB0 identity (emergent.py:196) excludes the tempo factor, and at the 2023 start tau sits at its relaxation target so realized dtau ~ 0 and the tempo factor ~ 1; hence model quantum*fec = TFR_2023 at the anchor BY CONSTRUCTION (Korea: 0.72). Published adjTFR embeds the observed postponement (Korea 1.005, gaps +0.11..+0.23), so the model can never land near the published levels at/near 2023 for any kBF - the synthesis's own claim that 'the model's C*(1-rv)*Pb*fec at the Korea anchor must land near 1.0' is contradicted by the model's arithmetic. The whole 2023 tempo gap is currently absorbed into PB0 as quantum.
findings.fix: Score the GAP dynamics, not levels: with tau anchored to the observed MAC path in the backtest (secTau/kTau refit in Stage 3 so in-window dtau ~ 0.09-0.23 yr/yr), test G_model = kBF*dtau against observed G = 1-TFR/adjTFR per region-year. Alternatively re-anchor quantum to adjTFR at 2023 and let the tempo term carry the observed gap - but that is a structural re-anchoring of the PB0 identity and must be declared as such, not slipped in as Stage 4.

findings.item: PB0_check acceptance bar (|PB0-PB0_check|/PB0 < 10%) mechanically fails for USA (~37%) and Korea (~20%) for epoch reasons, not composition error
findings.why: PB0 = TFR_2023/(C0(1-RV0)fec) is a PERIOD-quantum parity, deflated by the 2023 tempo/quantum erosion the identity buries in it; PB0_check = CFR_1975/((1-p0)fec) is a COHORT parity of women reproducing ~1995-2015. Computed: USA PB0=1.936 vs check=2.659 (37%); Korea 1.642 vs ~1.97 (20%); Italy ~9%, Germany ~4%. The gap IS the CFR-minus-period-TFR signal the deliverable elsewhere assigns to secPb/secC/kBF - so the diagnostic double-counts that signal as 'quantum composition wrong for that region' and the protocol's instruction to 'log it, do not tune it away' would log a spurious model indictment for the two regions with the largest tempo/erosion gaps.
findings.fix: Compare like with like: either integrate the backtested model over the 1975 cohort's reproductive window and compare integrated cohort quantities (CFR_model vs CFR_obs, parity-of-mothers_model vs check), or period-deflate CFR using the tempo family before differencing. Set the 10% bar on the epoch-matched comparison only; report the raw period-vs-cohort gap separately as the erosion signal it is.

findings.item: The protocol's headline honesty metric is wrong: |PB_SCALE_ENS - 1| does not absorb anchor error and will not shrink after re-anchoring
findings.why: PB_SCALE_ENS is solved so the DISPERSED ensemble matches the scalar anchor (calibrate_ens, emergent.py:637-650); the scalar anchor is exact for ANY (C0,RV0,tau) because the PB0 identity absorbs all anchor error into PB0. Hence |PB_SCALE_ENS-1| (1.016-1.037) measures only the Jensen/clip gap from SIGMA_CAL dispersion - approximately invariant to anchor correctness. The protocol's expectation that it 'must SHRINK' after re-anchoring is baseless; when it doesn't shrink, the stated interpretation ('the new anchors conflict with the 2023 TFR ... being re-buried') would produce a false alarm on every region.
findings.fix: Replace the honesty metric: track PB0 itself (the actual absorber) against the epoch-matched PB0_check per stage, plus the count of regions whose PB0 moves toward the independent parity-of-mothers value. Keep |PB_SCALE_ENS-1| only as a dispersion-sanity check with a no-growth (not shrink) criterion.

findings.item: The Poland 'infeasibility proof' (C0[PL] must rise to >= 0.897) rides entirely on the family's own weakest number
findings.why: It uses p0=0.103 (GGS survey, small n, cohorts 1965-71 at 40-44 - the OLDEST cohorts of the window), while the family itself documents HFD rising to 0.20 by the 1974 cohort and brackets the true late-window value at 0.10-0.20. At p0=0.18 the feasibility floor is 0.82 - exactly the current hand-set C0. A 'proof' whose conclusion flips within the stated measurement bracket is not a proof, and 'Poland UP' is promoted from plausible (supported independently by the union-share rank) to mandated on that basis.
findings.fix: Downgrade to 'directionally supported, magnitude unresolved' until the GUS NSP 2021 census cohort-parity table (kobiety wedlug liczby urodzonych dzieci) is read - the GUS-preference convention demands it anyway. Only then re-run the feasibility arithmetic.

findings.item: The trapped norm well Nhi=0.42 is 'confirmed' by zero valid observations; option B would launder a definitional artifact into a structural constant
findings.why: The sole quantitative match (Korea 0.426 vs Nhi 0.42) is an INTENTION share (KPPIF private survey, N=2000, read via Korea Herald), while the family's construct is IDEAL-zero; its own caveat states intentions read systematically HIGH vs ideals (Japan instruments span 1.2-40.3% on wording alone). Under a consistent ideal-zero definition Korea would likely read well below 0.42, leaving NO region in the high well - yet option B proposes to relocate Nhi to ~0.43 'pinned by Korea'. Every other region sits an order of magnitude below its assigned well, so the current double-well geometry has no surviving observational support on this panel.
findings.fix: Adopt option A strictly (ordering-only latent index) and delete the 'sits exactly on the model's Nhi well' claim from the calibration narrative - it is a coincidence across incompatible instruments. Research gap: obtain a Korean ideal-zero share from a national instrument (KOSIS social survey / KIHASA National Fertility Survey ideal-children distribution) before any well relocation is even considered.

findings.item: Option A is not behaviour-preserving as written: any NORM0 value off the exact well positions breaks the baseline fixed point
findings.why: Baseline neutrality requires NORM0[r] to equal a stable well (Nlo/Nhi) exactly - that is what makes lam_rho*(N-NORM0) identically zero (emergent.py:79-90, :225). If the 'latent norm index calibrated on ordering' is written into the NORM0 dict as intermediate values, N relaxes to the nearest well while NORM0 stays put, lam_rho*(N-NORM0) goes nonzero, and rv acquires a permanent secular drift; PB_SCALE_ENS (solved at years=1) re-passes the anchor guard while every baseline trajectory and E25-E39 norm verdict silently shifts - precisely the outcome option A exists to avoid.
findings.fix: State explicitly in Stage 0(d): under option A the code's NORM0 dict is untouched; the latent index and its monotone link to survey shares live only in the documentation/mapping table (calibration_targets.csv rows flagged ordering-only). Any change to NORM0 values = option B and triggers the re-verdict gate.

findings.item: Protocol collides with the E40 pytest guard suite and misquotes its anchor bar
findings.why: tests/test_hypothesis_guards.py asserts PARAMS['kBF'] == 0.6 (test_guard_kbf_documented_value) - Stage 4 moving kBF to any other value fails make test; test_guard_e19_tempo_mirage_amplitude pins the tempo bump to (0.03, 0.15), a band derived AT kBF=0.6 and sensitive to the Stage-1 tau re-pin; test_guard_e37_h363 pins the Korea transplant lift to (0.6, 0.9) and test_guard_e36/e15 pin lever orderings - all encode verdict numbers under the CURRENT anchors. Stage 5's re-verdict gate enumerates notebooks/headlines but never the guard suite. Also Stage 2 claims '< 1e-4 for 8/8 (the existing bar)' - the actual guard bar is 5e-4 (test line 56), and the committed 4-decimal PB_SCALE_ENS values only support ~5e-4; demanding 1e-4 against them would spuriously fail.
findings.fix: Add to Stage 5 an explicit guard-suite re-baselining step: enumerate every numeric band in tests/test_hypothesis_guards.py, re-derive each under the new anchors, and update assertions in the same change (user-approved) - a kBF move additionally updates the documented-value guard and the E40 doc paragraph it references. Correct Stage 2's acceptance to the real 5e-4 bar.

findings.item: Stage 3 WLS noise model (s_TFR = 0.03) is misspecified against admitted structural model error, so the global-drift fit and any rejection verdicts are uninterpretable
findings.why: The synthesis concedes the model cannot produce Germany's 2005-2016 hump (amplitude ~0.26 = ~8.7 sigma per point over ~10 annual points) or Japan's double sign change, yet those years enter the loss at sigma=0.03. The fit of {secC, secPb, secTau, kTau} will be dominated by episodes the model is declared unable to fit, dragging the global drifts to compromise values that mis-fit the regions the model CAN explain (Italy's clean monotone slide, the Korea descent) - and chi-square-scale statements become meaningless because sigma encodes only source noise, not structural error.
findings.fix: Either add a structural-error term to sigma (s_eff^2 = s_source^2 + s_struct^2 with s_struct ~ 0.08-0.10, stated), or restrict the WLS to episodes/regions inside the model's declared mechanism scope and keep the unfittable features exclusively in the pass/fail Tier-2 battery (already their role). Use a robust loss (Huber) if mixed. State which option in the protocol before fitting.

findings.item: The partnership 8-way ranking is over-resolved for its harmonisation error, and the proposed affine's Israel endpoint is unmeasured
findings.why: FR and USA values are both-sexes (male partnership at 25-39 runs lower/later, biasing vs women-only cells), USA is 25-34, KR is 30-39 ever-married, IL is 25-29 ever-married - adjacent gaps in the claimed ordering (USA 0.57 vs JP 0.535; FR 0.642 vs PL ~0.63) are smaller than the family's own +-0.05-0.10 harmonisation error, so only the extremes (KR bottom, IL top) and the large Poland/Italy separations are rank-safe. Worse, the two-point affine C0 = a + b*u requires u_IL, which was never obtained (only ages 25-29 = 0.553 exists) - the proposed map cannot be constructed from the data in hand.
findings.fix: Restrict rank claims to the harmonisation-safe ones (KR lowest, IL highest, PL > IT, JP > IT); fetch the KOSIS 2020 census 25-39 currently-married-by-sex cut and the CBS Statistical Abstract marital-status-by-age table to build harmonized u for KR/IL before parameterising any map (which per the BLOCKER should target the lifetime construct anyway).

findings.item: Israel - the null-control region - has the thinnest independent evidence base of the 8, and its advertised 'dead on' childlessness match is not a validation
findings.why: The 0.078 covers cohorts 1947-1967 (entirely outside the 1965-78 window) and the national total was read from an advocacy-outlet secondary (Hungarian Conservative) citing the Taub study; with childlessness rising secularly everywhere, in-window Israeli cohorts likely read higher, so the exact match to 1-C0(1-RV0)=0.0785 is a coincidence of vintages. Beyond that, Israel's CFR (WPP diagonal), TFR series (WPP), and MAC (WPP) all reduce to the single producer the Leslie layer already consumes, and Israel is null on adjTFR and childfree-norms and weakest on partnership (25-29 only) - so the region anchoring the untrapped basin and the C0=0.97/RV0=0.05 extremes is validated almost entirely by WPP self-consistency.
findings.fix: Demote the Israel childlessness row from 'dead on' to 'consistent, wrong-cohort, secondary-sourced'; fetch CBS census/register parity tables for cohorts born ~1965-78, the CBS Statistical Abstract marriage-by-age curve, and CBS vital-statistics cohort fertility so at least two Israel families rest on a non-WPP national primary.

findings.item: Mixed vintages/definitions inside single family records will corrupt naive ingestion
findings.why: Germany tempo record: the value field is EDS-2022 total-data BF (gap -0.04) while the attached series is the HFD by-order lineage ending 2016 (gap +0.05, opposite sign) - concatenating value onto series fabricates a trend reversal. Poland tempo gap is internally consistent to HFD raw TFR (1.327, 2021) and NOT to the campaign's GUS anchor (1.16, 2023) - differencing adjTFR against GUS raw would misstate the tempo signal by ~0.15. The BF vs TFRp* variant split (up to 0.15 apart, USA) is flagged in notes but nothing structural prevents a downstream consumer mixing them.
findings.fix: When building reports/calibration_targets.csv, give each row an explicit (producer, variant, vintage) key and forbid cross-key differencing in the loader: Poland tempo rows scored only within HFD-internal pairs; Germany carries two separate rows (HFD-by-order-2016, EDS-BF-2022) with the sign disagreement recorded, never one merged series.

findings.item: 2000-era init cells 'solved by shooting to the 2023 anchor' contribute far more than 'shape information only'
findings.why: With relaxation timescales of ~12-20 years (kC=0.08, kPb=0.05, kTau=0.06), an initial condition chosen to hit the 2023 endpoint largely determines the entire 2000-2015 trajectory of that channel - the region's Tier-1 path score is then substantially a function of the fitted init, i.e. circular, and down-weighting it as 'shape only' understates how much of the apparent fit is inherited from the shooting step.
findings.fix: Exclude shot-init region-channels from the Tier-1 WLS entirely (they may still appear in Tier-2 pass/fail features that do not depend on the init, e.g. the Korea-only trap-firing criterion which is about 2015-2023 curvature), and report per-region which cells were shot so the circularity boundary is explicit in the deliverable table.

findings.item: The entire q (marriageability capital) state and its E30 block have ZERO observational contact
findings.why: q is a full 7th channel with its own dynamics (kq=0.06, gqC=0.9, phi=0.4, gA=0.5, wF=0.6, wScar=0.5, lagLo=27, lagHi=45, childhood=18) plus the CohortMemory intergenerational path. The synthesis itself states gqC*q is identically zero at baseline (q starts 0, env is intervention-only, emergent.py:291-293/442/615), so NO family touches it and it appears in NO predicted-vs-observed row. Yet GOAL-12/E22 crowns marriageable-men as 'the strongest causal lever, the ONLY lever that bends Korea.' A campaign headline rides on a state with no anchor. The harness would expose q_t but there is nothing to compare it to.
findings.fix: Add a marriageable-men family: (a) sex ratio at reproductive ages and (b) a male-economic-prospects index (prime-age male employment/participation and real median male earnings) per region 2000-2023, and map q(2000) and the gqC gain onto it. Sources: OECD/ILO male employment rates 25-44; national earnings series (BLS, Eurostat earn_, KOSIS, CBS, e-Stat); WPP SRB on disk. The E22 citations (Autor China-shock, Kearney-Wilson fracking) already imply the elasticity (0.2-0.4) that pins gqC.

findings.item: Migration is identically zero in the behavioural core and no family covers it, though net-migration data sits on disk
findings.why: emergent.py multiplies the Rogers-Castro profile by 0.0 (leslie_step migration term), and no research family targets migration. For Israel and the USA (and increasingly Germany/Italy) net migration is a first-order driver of the population trajectory and age structure that feeds dep_pen -> S. The only returned population observable (pop_pct) is therefore structurally biased for high-migration regions, and any 2000-2023 population/pyramid backtest cannot validate. demographic_indicators.csv already carries NetMigrations and CNMR per region-year, entirely unused.
findings.fix: Either wire the on-disk WPP NetMigrations/CNMR series into the Leslie layer for the backtest and add a net-migration-rate family (WPP CNMR on disk; national: CBS, Destatis Wanderungen, ONS-equivalent), or explicitly scope population-trajectory claims as migration-free and drop pop_pct from the validated surface. Do not leave migration silently zeroed while claiming checkable population predictions.

findings.item: Annual birth COUNTS - the most-published vital statistic - have no family, yet the harness leans on births_t
findings.why: The harness spec names births_t as 'the single most-published vital statistic in every region' and the model computes then DISCARDS it (_b binding at emergent.py:300/427/603). No research family delivers observed annual births 2024-2025. Birth counts are the cleanest out-of-sample test of the whole composition x Leslie layer (TFR alone hides the age-structure multiplier). This is the cheapest, hardest validation left unfilled.
findings.fix: Add an annual-births family 2019-2025: NCHS (USA), MHLW Vital Statistics (Japan), KOSIS (Korea), GUS (Poland), CBS 178,724 for 2023 (Israel), Destatis + Eurostat demo_fasec (FR/DE/IT). Several 2023/2024 counts already surfaced during target research (Japan 727,277; Israel 178,724) - consolidate them into a checkable row per region-year.

findings.item: Parity distribution is null for 5 of 8 regions (France, Italy, Korea, Poland, Israel)
findings.why: The completed-cohort-fertility-parity family verified an actual 0/1/2/3+ split for only USA, Germany, Japan. The PB0_check = CFR/((1-p0)*fec) degeneracy-breaker (the whole point of that family - separating parity from C0/RV0) therefore has real independent parity data for only 3/8 regions; for the other 5 it collapses back onto the CFR level alone, and Korea+Israel CFRs are themselves WPP diagonals (not independent of the model's own Leslie backbone).
findings.fix: Fetch cohort parity distributions: INSEE 'repartition des femmes selon le nombre d'enfants' by generation (France); ISTAT percorsi-generazioni / demo.istat.it FE1 (Italy); KOSIS 2020 Census 'children ever born', ever-married caveat (Korea); GUS NSP 2021 'kobiety wedlug liczby urodzonych dzieci' (Poland, GUS-preference); CBS women-by-number-of-children tables (Israel). HFD cohort parity tables (auth-gated) are the cross-region upgrade path.

findings.item: Israel is unscored on TWO whole families (tempo-adjusted-TFR and childfree-norms)
findings.why: Israel is the only region oscillating ~3.0 - the designated null control for the coupling trap - yet it has no published Bongaarts-Feeney adjTFR (absent from HFD/HFC/EDS) and no located childfree-ideal share (value=null). The null control cannot exercise the kBF tempo check or the NORM0 assignment it is supposed to anchor, weakening exactly the region that disciplines false positives.
findings.fix: adjTFR: seek Okun's academic decompositions of Israeli fertility tempo vs quantum (Demography/Population Studies) or compute B-F from CBS single-age ASFR + MAC change. childfree-norms: CBS Social Survey 2019+ family module table generator, or DellaPergola 2005 attitudes microdata for the zero tail.

findings.item: The norm double-well stiffness aN and tipping point thN are unobservable from static shares, and no childfree-ideal TIME SERIES exists
findings.why: The synthesis admits aN (well stiffness) needs a norm-change time series that does not exist and thN (the 0.25 tipping point) is likewise unconstrained. Worse, option B (well relocation) - a structural change forcing E25-E39 verdict re-runs - would peg Nhi=0.42 on a SINGLE Korea intention survey (KPPIF via Korea Herald) whose wording reads high vs ideal-zero. The bistable norm geometry, which drives all norm-intervention verdicts, is anchored by essentially one contested point.
findings.fix: Build a childfree-ideal / intended-childlessness panel from repeated waves: Eurobarometer 2001/2006/2011 (Testa; the discontinued module still gives 3 EU points), GGS-I/II, German FReDA 2021-2024, plus Korea's KIHASA/Presidential-Committee repeat surveys. Even a 3-4 point trajectory per region constrains aN and thN and replaces the single-survey Nhi peg.

findings.item: The age-fecundity decay slope (0.03/yr above 30) and the hardcoded age-30 knee are load-bearing but anchored by no family, and the Delta1 entry-age decision is unresolved
findings.why: fec(tau)=exp(-0.03*max(tau-30,0)) and gRV*max(tau-30,0) both key childlessness and fecundity off a biological threshold at age 30, applied to tau which the synthesis proves is mean age at CHILDBEARING (2-4 yr above first-birth age), not entry age. No family targets the 0.03 slope or the 30 knee, and the synthesis defers the Delta1 (MAC-vs-MAB1 keying) fork as a documented limitation - meaning the childlessness channel keeps running on semantics the threshold was arguably not written for.
findings.fix: Anchor the fecundability-by-age curve to natural-fertility / ART-adjusted studies (e.g. age-specific fecundability from Eijkemans, Leridon, or the ASFR right-tail decline observable in fertility_by_age1.csv on disk), and resolve Delta1 with the OECD SF2.3 MAB1 vs WPP MAC gap already tabulated (0.5 yr Korea to 3.2 yr Israel) so the knee is keyed to a named observable.

findings.item: Old-age dependency ratio has no observed family, yet dep_t feeds the dep_fb security feedback and the harness exposes it
findings.why: dep = pop(65+)/pop(20-64) drives dep_pen = dep_fb*max(dep-dep0,0), the channel through which ageing suppresses S. The harness proposes exposing dep_t, but no research family provides the OBSERVED dependency-ratio series to check it against, so the one endogenous feedback linking the Leslie layer back into behaviour is unvalidated on the data side.
findings.fix: Add an old-age-dependency family from WPP (Q-series / age pyramids already in population_by_age1.csv on disk) and Eurostat demo_pjanind (OADR) 2000-2023 per region - a near-free fill from on-disk and standard sources; the dep_fb GAIN itself stays a latent elasticity (see the fix_type=none finding).

findings.item: SIGMA_CAL population-heterogeneity spreads are declared 'structural not fit' but only tau's 3yr is anchored; C, rv, Pb, S, N, q spreads have no observable
findings.why: The dispersed ensemble (run_cal, the production scorer) depends on per-channel marginal SDs (C 0.05, rv 0.03, Pb 0.15, S 0.10, N 0.06, q 0.10). Only the tau SD ~3yr is tied to a named empirical quantity. The rest are judgment, and the protocol freezes SIGMA_CAL untouched - so the ensemble spread that generates every heterogeneity claim and the dist_end marginals is uncalibrated on 6 of 7 channels.
findings.fix: Ground the spreads in observed cross-sectional dispersion: parity distribution variance -> Pb and rv spread (from the parity-distribution family once filled); age-at-birth SD -> tau (already ~3yr); union-status variance -> C. S/N/q spreads remain judgment and should be flagged as such rather than presented as structural.

findings.item: The defection parameter delta has no observable target and is intervention-specific
findings.why: delta (net = gross*(1-delta) - backfire*delta) is folded per-entry into 187 catalogue forcings and can flip an intervention's sign. It governs behavioural gaming of policy (tutoring bans -> private tutoring). It is not a single global constant and no family covers it. It is weakly researchable from natural experiments but only per-mechanism, not as a calibratable model parameter.
findings.fix: Where a specific lever's verdict hinges on its delta (bans, wealth caps, quotas), cite the natural-experiment elasticity behind that delta in the intervention's provenance (e.g. Korea 2008 hagwon-curfew evasion for tutoring bans) rather than treating delta as a tunable knob; otherwise mark delta as an assumed policy-response prior, not a calibrated quantity.

findings.item: S0's level, the dep_fb gain, and gTau/gS_C are structurally unobservable at baseline - the plan can operationalise but not fit them
findings.why: The synthesis is honest that S0 is a pure gauge at baseline (only S-S0 deviations enter), so no data can FIT it - the co-residence family only orders/spaces it. Likewise dep_fb converts an observable (dependency ratio) into an unobservable latent (security perception) via a gain with no measurable counterpart, and gTau/gS_C are exercised only under crisis excursions. Any documentation language saying these were 'calibrated' would overclaim.
findings.fix: State explicitly in the calibration surface that S0 is operationalised (co-residence ordering) not fitted; that dep_fb, gTau, gS_C, aN are internal latent gains identified only weakly (crisis episodes) or not at all; keep them in the companion 'unanchored constants' section of the predicted-vs-observed table so the surface's observational boundary is explicit.

findings.item: Intervention-forcing weights (wF, wScar, phi, gA) and the CohortMemory lags are calibrated by nothing
findings.why: fF (father-access) and fScar (relationship-scar) are intervention-only (zero at baseline), so 'no baseline observable' is expected - but the WEIGHTS that scale them into env = wF*(fF+phi*q) - wScar*fScar and the intergenerational lags (lagLo=27, lagHi=45, gA=0.5, childhood=18) determine intervention magnitude and timing with no empirical anchor, undermining the credibility of any E30-memory intervention verdict's size/lag.
findings.fix: Anchor gA and the lags to intergenerational-fertility-transmission literature (mother-daughter completed-fertility correlations ~0.1-0.2; the ~27-45 reproductive window is demographically fixed) and cite a divorce/parental-conflict scarring effect size for wScar; if none can be sourced, flag these as assumed structural weights, not calibrated.

findings.item: The mortality-improvement rate (0.3%/yr, global) and fixed 2023 SRB are hardcoded, not fit to regional life-expectancy trends
findings.why: Sx = 1-(1-Sx0)*(1-0.003)^(yr+1) applies one global mortality-improvement rate to all 8 regions, and SRB is frozen at 2023. Regional life-expectancy trajectories differ materially (Korea vs USA post-2020), and life_table_both.csv (Sx) plus demographic_indicators.csv (LEx series) are on disk and unused for this. Low severity because it lives in the Leslie layer and mainly affects the age pyramid, not the behavioural TFR.
findings.fix: If pyramid/population backtest accuracy matters, fit per-region mortality improvement to WPP LEx 2000-2023 (on disk) instead of the 0.3%/yr global constant; SRB is regionally near-constant so freezing it is defensible.

findings.item: PARAMS['wS']=0.3 is dead code and should be flagged for removal
findings.why: Confirmed by grep: emergent.py:147 is the sole occurrence of wS; env uses wF and wScar (lines 293/442/615), never wS. It is a dropped security-weight from the E30 design. Not a calibration gap per se, but it pollutes the parameter inventory the completeness table must enumerate and could mislead a future calibrator into seeking an observable for a no-op.
findings.fix: Flag wS=0.3 for removal in Stage 0 (the synthesis already notes this); no behaviour change. Not a research target.

critiques.verdict: The synthesis is strong and honest on the seven channel anchors it set out to reground (C0, RV0, tau/MAC, NORM0, S0, PB0, plus the trajectory/tempo/marriage witnesses), and its own risk section pre-empts several degeneracies. But as a COMPLETENESS matter it leaves material blind spots: (1) an entire introduced state - q/marriageability, the E30 block that GOAL-12 calls the strongest causal lever - has zero observational contact and appears in no predicted-vs-observed row; (2) migration is identically zeroed in the core while NetMigrations/CNMR sit unused on disk, so population/pyramid predictions are structurally unvalidatable for Israel/USA; (3) annual birth counts, the most-published vital statistic and the natural out-of-sample test, have no family though the model computes and discards them. Beyond these, parity distributions are null for 5/8 regions (crippling the PB0 degeneracy-breaker), Israel (the null control) is unscored on two whole families, the bistable-norm geometry (aN, thN, Nhi) rests on essentially one contested Korea survey with no time series, and the biological fec/age-30 machinery plus most SIGMA_CAL spreads are unanchored. A cluster of gains (S0 level, dep_fb, gTau/gS_C, aN, intervention weights) is structurally unobservable and must be labelled operationalised/latent, not calibrated. Verdict: the checkable surface covers the composition's static anchors well but does NOT yet make 'predictions checkable per parameter' - roughly a third of the introduced parameters, one whole state, and the migration driver remain unobserved. Fillable gaps dominate over structurally-unobservable ones.
